title: Dragging a component from the Library drops one copy, not two
goal: You reported on 2026-09-29 that dragging a component off the Library drops two copies. Reproduced at Next defaults: nothing fires twice, but the first drag lands your copy and the component's original beside it, and on a video that makes two tracks. Where the original should live instead is on the card; once it is answered, one drag makes exactly one new layer.
acceptance: Reproduced first: a walk at Next defaults drags a component tile from the Library onto the canvas with the pointer, and onto a video's timeline, and counts the new layers; the report names the handler(s) that fire
One drag and drop makes exactly one new layer (one component instance) wherever it lands, as one undo step
The drop lands where the pointer let go (canvas point, or timeline track and time), and Esc during the drag cancels it with nothing added
A test drives the drop handler path twice-safely: a drop delivered to overlapping targets inserts once
The same check is run for every other Library shelf that can be dragged (media, styles) and any double drop there is fixed too

log.note: Reproduced. component-drag-lands-a-copy-walk (Next defaults, Button starter): first drop takes the layer count 1 -> 3 (rows Button, Button, Background); second drop 3 -> 4. component-on-the-timeline-walk (sample recording): first insert 1 -> 3 with two bars on two tracks (Button 2 and Button), one undo step (undo 3 -> 1); second drop 3 -> 4. So nothing fires twice: the second drawing is the component's ORIGINAL, which insertStarterComponent / insertSharedComponent bring in beside the copy on the first drop of a tile (1beb145e, from the 2026-09-20 answer 'Always a copy', whose own con was 'A drawing you did not ask for appears beside your drop the first time').

Handlers: only CanvasNSView registers com.photonz.component-id (CanvasDrop.performDragOperation -> onDropComponent -> EditorState.placeComponent, once). TimelineFileDropDelegate, WindowFileDrop and PanelFileDrop take FileDrop.types (+transition) only, so no second surface can take a component; AppKit hands a drop to one destination. A REAL pointer drag could not be driven from here: this terminal is not Accessibility-trusted (AXIsProcessTrusted false) and a walk cannot run a real NSDraggingSession (pickUpTile refuses the session by design). Other shelves: Media tile drag onto a layer row adds one layer (document-media-walk 2 -> 3); a text style drop adds no layers. No double drop there.

Reproduced at Next defaults: nothing fires twice. The first drag of a tile lands the copy AND the component's original beside it (from the 2026-09-20 'Always a copy' answer), which on a video also makes two tracks. Where the original should live instead is a UX call: decision card opened, recommending the original stay out of the picture and open on its own via Edit Original.
